messages:
maria: Heads up — planning a CMK rotation for prod snapshot objects next Tue 02:00 UTC. Need to lock down RBAC changes for the backup-uploader service account and make sure audit trail can't be rewritten. Any objections?
kevin: Why rotate at the snapshot object level instead of rotating the CMK only and leaving objects as-is?
samir: Because some customers have per-tenant CMKs; we need to re-encrypt objects to the new CMK identifier for compliance. We also want to switch to ephemeral delegated grants instead of long-lived cross-account grants.
anna-sec: +1 on ephemeral grants. Major caveat: re-encrypt workflows often replace metadata in-place which can erase original key/grant references. That would break forensic trails. Do not mutate audit fields.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: create a new object with new SSE-KMS key, copy metadata + append a signed_original_metadata block with original key id + grant id hashed, then mark old object as superseded.
kevin: Storage cost spike during rotation window — ops needs to approve. How long we keep both copies?
samir: Plan: keep both for 7 days, GC after successful canary restores. For tenants with long restores, allow opt-out with escrow process.
kevin: What about the grant-prune job? It prunes KMS grants hourly. If we create ephemeral grants for the uploader and then prune too early, restores could fail.
anna-sec: Good catch. Either extend grant TTL for rotation or use a dedicated long-restore grant path. For audit we should log grant creation + grant-id in centralized audit index.
maria: Quick POC of the S3 copy step (aws cli) I've been testing:
```
aws s3 cp s3://snapshots/prod/snap-2025-03-20.db \n  s3://snapshots/prod/snap-2025-03-20.db.reenc \n  --metadata-directive REPLACE \
  --sse aws:kms \
  --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/NEW-CMK-UUID \
  --metadata signed_original_key_id=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/OLD-CMK-UUID,signed_original_grant_id=GRNT-abc123
```
Note: copy to a new key/name first, verify integrity and audit entries, then atomically swap pointers in our metadata service.
kevin: We should add a verification step that checks the signed_original_metadata hash before we accept the new object. Also emit a separate audit event: snapshot.reencrypt.completed with both key ids.
encops-bot: runbook created: https://encops.internal/runbooks/cmk-rotation-snapshots (canary docs + checklist). Scheduled canary: Tue 01:30 UTC — will run full restore of 3 sample tenants.
samir: Also need RBAC change: backup-uploader SA will get kms:Encrypt kms:Decrypt for NEW-CMK and a Tag-based condition so it only decrypts objects with tag reencrypt-in-progress=false. That avoids accidental reads during swap.
anna-sec: Make sure the CloudTrail events preserve original kmsKeyId in the event records. If our copy path causes CloudTrail to log only the new key, we must capture original_key_id in our app-level audit event.
maria: I'll open a PR to encops playbook with these requirements: non-destructive re-encrypt (copy-to-new), signed_original_metadata, dual-audit events, TTL/GCL window, and grant-ttl adjustments. I'll add a canary test that intentionally prunes grants to ensure the failover path works.
kevin: Ops — can you confirm capacity bump for the 24h rotation window? We may need 1.5x storage temporarily.
encops-bot: canary run scheduled Tue 01:30 UTC. Notifying oncall: @oncall-encops.
maria: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link once ready and tag @anna-sec for review.
